chunks: Another text: Al-Mudhaffar ibn Ja'far al-Alawi al-Samarqandi - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ood al-Ayyashi narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: Yusuf ibn al-Sakht narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Qasim al-Uraydhi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Haydar ibn Ayyoub, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Hashemi, that he said:

The Shiites will now accept Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both) as Imam. I said: How is that? He said: Abul Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) called him and appointed him as his Testamentary Trustee.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abul Hasan (a title for Musa ibn Ja'far)

ai.seo_question: Who appointed Imam Ali ibn Musa as the next Imam according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the explicit designation (tawqi') of Imam Ali al-Rida by his father, Imam Musa al-Kazim, establishing the continuity of the Imamate within the progeny of Imam al-Kazim. It serves as a key proof for the Shi'a doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation), illustrating how the Imams formally appointed their successors to ensure communal unity and clarity of leadership during the era of the Abbasid caliphate.
